newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS Cargo 300 mln skr below 1996 target.
newsitem.headline: SAS Cargo 300 mln skr below 1996 target.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS's cargo operations' contribution to the bottom line profit for the airline fell 300 million crowns short of a target for 1996, a spokesman for SAS Cargo said on Tuesday.
"We were 300 million crowns off target," Jens Justesen, spokesman for SAS cargo division, told Reuters.
For 1997, The cargo division has set a sales target of 1.85 billion crowns for 1997, an increase of 100 million crowns, he said.

The airline also set a goal to sell 90 tonnes capacity on its Boeing 747-200 freighter which flies twice weekly to the Far East and once a week to New York from the Swedish west coast city of Gothenburg, Justesen said.
It also planned to cut costs by moving the SAS Cargo headquarters to Stockholm's Arlanda airport from their current location near the centre of the Swedish capital, he added.
SAS Cargo planned to move its other administration offices to airports in Oslo and Copenhagen, he said.
"We will introduce a flatter organisation which will be closer to the business," Peter Gronlund, head of the cargo division at SAS, told Swedish business daily Dagens Industri.

"At the same time we must move closer to the customers so we understand their needs. Customer contact now lies entirely with the cargo forwarders, but we will change that," he was quoted as saying by Dagens Industri.
The Scandinavian airline, in part owned by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway, has an 18 percent market share of air cargo out of Scandinavia, Justesen said.
This means its market share is about the same as its partner's, Lufthansa Cargo, he said.
